depth_justification: Severe verbatim looping: the identical four-dimension block (DHA, clinical evidence, GDPR, FHIR/ELGA interoperability) is repeated five times with no new information, the citations are loose or wrong (labels a smoking-cessation coach 'SaMD' with 'clinical features' then flatly reverses), and it never engages QuitNow's actual salient risks (peer-feed harm, gamification of vulnerable smokers).
actionability_justification: Mostly generic platitudes ('implement GDPR-compliant data handling', 'avoid medical claims'); the final report adds a couple of thinly relevant items (peer-support moderation/reporting, accessibility) but offers little concrete, implementable recipe.
salient_examples: Identical block 'Is QuitNow a digital health application (DHA)... [P4.D1] Interoperability (ANS, FHIR)... ELGA in Austria, DMP in France' repeated 5x verbatim
QuitNow is a software as a medical device (SaMD) because it ... includes clinical features (turn 1), then 'does not fall under the definition of a medical device' (turn 2)
Implement GDPR-compliant data handling, including data encryption, anonymization, and user consent mechanisms
Peer support features may expose users to misinformation ... Implement moderation tools, user reporting systems
